message.content:
The function reads an attacker-controlled `body_len`, computes `encoded_len = body_len + pad`, and checks `encoded_len > wire_left - 4` before `memcpy(scratch, body, encoded_len)`.

The bug: `scratch` is only `AUTH_STACK_MAX` (256) bytes, but `encoded_len` can be up to `wire_left - 4`, which may exceed 256. The check on line 17 only validates against the packet size, not against the stack buffer size — so a packet larger than 256 bytes causes a stack buffer overflow in the `memcpy` on line 20.

The primary bug is introduced at the `memcpy` where the unchecked-against-buffer-size copy occurs.

Answer: 20
